title: Free coordinates after fixing a list
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho$ be a coordinate restriction on $n$ coordinates, let $L$ be a nonempty list of coordinates, and let $x$ be a binary vector of length $n$. Suppose every coordinate in $L$ is free in $\rho$. After fixing the coordinates in $L$ according to the signs encoded by $x$, the number of free coordinates is strictly less than it was in $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: every listed coordinate is initially free
$x$ is a binary vector of length $n$
